note: Health-Body sample (10 words) in the extended format.

words.meaning: Good at sports or enjoying physical activity.
words.situation: He is very athletic because he plays soccer and runs every single morning.
words.gap: My sister is very ______ — she swims, plays tennis, and never gets tired.
hints: Describes someone who is strong, fit, and good at sports.
Starts with 'ath-' and ends with '-ic'.

commonMistake.sentence: He is a very athlete person.
commonMistake.correction: He is a very athletic person.
commonMistake.why: 'Athlete' is a noun (the person); use the adjective 'athletic' to describe someone.

words.meaning: An injury in which a ligament is stretched or torn.
words.situation: He sprained his ankle during the match and had to sit out for a week.
words.gap: Be careful on the stairs — a bad ______ can keep you off your feet for weeks.
hints: An injury to a ligament, often in the ankle or wrist.
Starts with 'spr-' and rhymes with 'rain'.

commonMistake.sentence: I have a sprain in my back muscle from lifting weights.
commonMistake.correction: I have a strain in my back muscle from lifting weights.
commonMistake.why: A sprain hurts a ligament; a hurt muscle or tendon is a strain.

words.meaning: An injury in which a muscle or tendon is stretched or torn.
words.situation: He got a muscle strain in his back after lifting heavy boxes.
words.gap: Running without warming up can cause a ______ in your leg muscles.
hints: An injury to a muscle or tendon that was stretched too far.
Starts with 'str-' and rhymes with 'rain'.

commonMistake.sentence: She twisted her ankle and got a strain in the ligament.
commonMistake.correction: She twisted her ankle and got a sprain in the ligament.
commonMistake.why: A hurt ligament is a sprain; 'strain' is for muscles and tendons.

words.situation: She stayed at home because she was sick.
words.gap: I felt too ______ to go to work, so I called my manager and stayed in bed.
hints: How you feel when you have a cold, the flu, or another illness.
A four-letter word that starts with 's'.

commonMistake.sentence: I feel sickness today, so I'm staying home.
commonMistake.correction: I feel sick today, so I'm staying home.
commonMistake.why: 'Sick' is the adjective for how you feel; 'sickness' is the noun.

words.meaning: Small solid medicines taken by mouth, including tablets and capsules in everyday use.
words.situation: He takes blood pressure pills every morning without fail.
words.gap: The doctor told me to take two ______ after breakfast with a glass of water.
hints: Small solid medicines that you swallow.
A five-letter word that starts with 'p'.

commonMistake.sentence: I drank two pills for my headache.
commonMistake.correction: I took two pills for my headache.
commonMistake.why: We take or swallow pills; we drink liquids.

words.situation: I couldn't go to work — I was under the weather.
words.gap: Maya is feeling a bit ______ today, so she's staying home with a cup of tea.
hints: An informal way to say you feel slightly ill.
It starts with 'under'.

commonMistake.sentence: I'm feeling under the weathers today.
commonMistake.correction: I'm feeling under the weather today.
commonMistake.why: The idiom is fixed: 'weather' is always singular here.

words.meaning: To remain awake instead of going to bed.
words.situation: I stayed up until 3 AM watching a series and regretted it the next morning.
words.gap: Kids are allowed to ______ late on Friday nights to watch a movie.
hints: To not go to bed at your usual time.
A phrasal verb: 'stay' + the opposite of 'down'.

commonMistake.sentence: I woke up until midnight to finish my homework.
commonMistake.correction: I stayed up until midnight to finish my homework.
commonMistake.why: 'Wake up' means to stop sleeping; 'stay up' means to not go to bed.

words.meaning: Blood pressure that is too high.
words.situation: He was told to reduce salt and stress to control his hypertension.
words.gap: Too much salt and stress can lead to ______, so doctors check your blood pressure regularly.
hints: A medical word for blood pressure that is too high.
Starts with 'hyper-', which means 'too much'.

commonMistake.sentence: My grandfather has hypotension, so he must eat less salt.
commonMistake.correction: My grandfather has hypertension, so he must eat less salt.
commonMistake.why: Hypertension is high blood pressure; hypotension is low blood pressure.

words.meaning: A hard covering that supports and protects a broken bone while it heals.
words.situation: He wore a cast on his arm for six weeks after breaking it.
words.gap: After she broke her leg, the doctor put it in a ______ for two months.
hints: A hard cover that keeps a broken bone still while it heals.
A four-letter word that also means all the actors in a film.

commonMistake.sentence: The doctor put a bandage on his broken arm to keep the bone still for six weeks.
commonMistake.correction: The doctor put a cast on his broken arm to keep the bone still for six weeks.
commonMistake.why: A bandage is soft material; the hard cover that holds a broken bone still is a cast.

words.meaning: Safe and unharmed, especially after a journey or dangerous event.
words.situation: He had an accident but he was safe and sound.
words.gap: After a long flight through a storm, the family finally arrived home ______.
hints: Not hurt or damaged, especially after danger or a journey.
'Safe and ___' — the missing word also means 'noise'.

commonMistake.sentence: The kids came home sound and safe.
commonMistake.correction: The kids came home safe and sound.
commonMistake.why: Binomials have a fixed order: always 'safe and sound'.
